In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the carboxy-terminus of the D1 protein is crucial to the assembly of the manganese cluster of photosystem II and that the cluster may contain a manganese ligand that is a carboxylate residue in the carboxyl-terminal domain of the protein.
the D1 polypesite of photosystem II is a manganese cluster ligand and that the D2 polypeptide is a calcium ligand.
the carboxy terminal domain of the D2 polypeptide contains the binding sites for the manganese and calcium of photosystem II and that these sites are located in the region of residues 332-342.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carboxy-terminus of the D1 protein plays a major role in the assembly and/or stabilization of the manganese cluster and that His-337 is a likely candidate for a ligand of the cluster.
the manganese cluster of photosystem II is composed of four manganese atoms, one calcium ion, and four ligands, two of which are carboxylates and the other two are histidines.
the carboxy terminus of the D1 protein contains several residues that are crucial for the assembly and stability of the manganese-cluster and/or for the binding of manganese and/or calcium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carboxy-terminus of D1 is important for water oxidation, but it is not the only region of the D1 and CP47 polypeptides that is important.
the D1 carboxy-terminal region is a critical component of the water-oxidation complex.

the carboxy- terminus of the D1 protein is a major binding site for manganese and calcium ions and plays important roles in the assembly and stability of the manganese-cluster and in the catalytic cycle.
